title: Resumable Edge Streaming + Fallback SDK Playbook
content:
Context and motivation:
This doc collects an implementation-first playbook for a resumable streaming surface aimed at edge and low-bandwidth clients. Goal: make streaming-hosted API calls robust to intermittent connectivity and mobile constraints while preserving tool-calling and typed/structured output semantics. We need an SDK ergonomics pattern that reduces app-level glue code and a pragmatic fallback state machine that preserves developer intent (partial outputs, tool handshakes, idempotency).

Key goals (non-exhaustive):
- Reliable partial progress: clients can resume a stream without re-running the full LLM run when network drops.
- Tool call safety: tool invocation frames remain transactional and resumable (no duplicate side effects).
- Predictable latency/behavior for mobile and edge clients by allowing local progressive render and controlled fallback to non-streaming or trimmed responses.
- Minimal SDK surface: a few primitives that cover most use cases (connect/resume/commit/abort).
- Rich telemetry hooks to measure user-visible progress, retransmits, and tool invocation success/failure.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Hosted API supports streaming partial tokens and structured frames (JSON blocks for actions/tool-calls).
- Backwards compatibility: existing non-resumable SDKs will continue to function; resumable features can be opt-in via flags.
- Server stores minimal resumable checkpoints per request id for a limited TTL (configurable, default 10m).
- Tool calls may involve webhooks or server-side side-effects; we must prevent double-execution by providing idempotency tokens and commit semantics.

High-level API/contract (proposal):
1) Start call (client -> server)
- POST /v1/chat.stream: body includes client_hint {"resume_token": optional, "resumable": true|false, "client_id": GUID} and call metadata. Server returns: stream session id + initial checkpoint id.
- If resume_token provided, server attempts to attach existing checkpoint and stream the rest.

2) Stream frames (server -> client):
- FRAME types: [meta, token, action_start, action_payload, action_end, checkpoint, error, end]
- Checkpoint frames include: checkpoint_id, sequence_number, cursor_position. These are small and emitted at configurable intervals (eg every 200 tokens / 3s).
- action_start/action_end wrap tool calls; action_payload carries structured JSON (string-encoded).

3) Commit/Abort semantics:
- Server emits an action_end with "requires_commit": true for tool-calls that would cause external side-effects. The client must POST commit/abort with the checkpoint_id before TTL to trigger the actual webhook/external call. Without a commit, server keeps action in pending state and will not perform side-effects.
- Commit endpoint: POST /v1/stream/commit { checkpoint_id, client_signature }
- Abort endpoint: POST /v1/stream/abort { checkpoint_id }

SDK ergonomics (proposal patterns):
- High-level primitives (client SDK):
  - openStream(opts): returns a StreamHandle (async iterable of frames) and a resumeToken when available.
  - resumeStream(resumeToken): attaches to an existing session.
  - onAction(handle, callback): registers callbacks for action_start/action_payload/action_end; SDK will surface a ConfirmAction API that returns a commit token.
  - checkpoint() -> currentResumeToken: app-level can snapshot and persist token (to localStorage / keychain).
  - gracefulFallbackPolicy: enum {retry, reconnect, nonStreaming-fallback, shortened-response} with prebuilt heuristics.

- Example usage (mobile pseudo):
  const h = await client.openStream({resumable:true});
  for await (frame of h) {
    if (frame.type === 'token') render(frame.text);
    if (frame.type === 'action_start') showToolPlaceholder();
    if (frame.type === 'action_end' && frame.requires_commit) {
      // show UI to user to confirm side-effect
      const commit = await showConfirm();
      await client.commit(frame.checkpoint_id, {user_id});
    }
  }

Fallback state machine (edge cases):
- Client drop: when socket disconnects, SDK stores the last checkpoint_id + resumeToken locally and begins exponential reconnect attempts. If reconnect succeeds within TTL, SDK automatically calls resumeStream. If TTL expires, SDK can request a trimmed non-resumable re-run (best-effort) or surface a partial transcript to user.
- Conflicting commits: if multiple clients hold resume tokens for the same session (shared devices), commit must be guarded by server-side compare-and-swap on checkpoint_id + client_signature. Server returns 409 + winning_client_id when conflict occurs.
- Stale action payloads: server side validates action payloads against latest model outputs; if mismatch, return action_replay_required to client.

Telemetry (minimal required events):
- stream.created {client_id, session_id, model, requested_resumable}
- stream.checkpoint_emitted {session_id, checkpoint_id, seq}
- stream.resume_attempt {session_id, resume_token, success:true|false, latency_ms}
- stream.disconnect {session_id, reason}
- tool.pending_commit {session_id, checkpoint_id, tool_name}
- tool.commit {session_id, checkpoint_id, result_code}
- fallback.triggered {session_id, policy}
- ui.latency_to_first_token {session_id, ms}
- api.retry_count {session_id, count}

Telemetry should be emitted with token-level cost / latency labels so we can map UX regressions to unit economics. Add a flag to reduce telemetry volume for low-tier customers.

Security and privacy notes:
- Resume tokens must be short-lived and cryptographically bound to client_id; do not leak tokens in logs.
- Checkpoint payloads scrub PII unless the customer opts-in to storing richer context.
- For private deployments (VPC/private), default TTL and commit semantics should be configurable (enterprise may increase TTL to 24h).

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (canary): server-side & internal SDK (node + iOS) implement feature flag; internal apps validate resumable behavior. Duration 2 weeks.
- Phase 1 (limited beta): enable for selected customers (flagged) with explicit contract and support runbook. Monitor tool commit rates and duplicate execution attempts. Duration 4 weeks.
- Phase 2 (public opt-in): exposed to all customers as opt-in via header X-RWI-Resumable: true. Gather broad telemetry for 6 weeks.
- Phase 3 (opt-out): change default to on for new accounts and keep off for legacy by default; customer controls via console.

Acceptance criteria (KPIs to claim success):
- Resume success rate >= 95% within TTL for mobile networks (3G/4G intermittent losses).
- Tool duplicate-execution rate < 0.1% after commit guardrails.
- Median time-to-first-token within 150ms for warm sessions.
- Error/no-resume fallback correctness: user shows coherent partial transcript in >98% of disconnect events.
- Telemetry volume controllable; disabled for free-tier accounts by default.

Developer docs + SDK deliverables (MVP):
- Node and browser SDK exposes openStream/resumeStream/commit/abort APIs.
- iOS/Android minimal wrapper with local checkpoint persistence examples.
- App sample: chat-with-confirmable-actions (example showing commit UI).
- Postman/HTTP examples and sequence diagrams.

Operational considerations / runbook highlights:
- Monitoring: alerts when resume success rate drops below 90% or when commit 409 conflicts increase above baseline by 3x.
- Mitigation: temporarily disable resumable for a model pool, surface advisory in Console and support channels.
- Privacy incident: immediate rotate resume token signing keys and invalidate outstanding tokens.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Checkpoint frequency tuning: default 200 tokens vs time-based (3s) — run A/B to measure telemetry cost vs resume latency.
- How to handle long-running tool calls that require external human confirmation? (webhook vs deferred server-side action).
- Billing model: resumed streams may re-emit tokens — do we bill by unique tokens emitted or per-request attempt? (Product needs guidance from finance).
- Should commits require a user-visible 2nd factor for high-impact tools? Policy question.

Next steps:
- Tech spike: implement prototype in internal SDKs (node/browser/iOS) and integrate with existing streaming runtime checkpoint emitters (ENG: serving-runtime & platform-engineering). Owner: Ethan Miller. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Product: circulate draft to Solutions Eng and Customer Success for beta candidate selection. Owner: Priya Kapoor. ETA: 1 week.
- Legal/Security: review commit semantics and PII scrubbing. Owner: Jared Wong. ETA: 1 week.

Notes to self / working fragments:
- Keep action commit TTL shorter than session TTL to avoid long-lived pending effects.
- Consider lightweight client-side signing of commit requests to reduce accidental commits from stolen resume tokens.
- Add a compatibility shim: SDK exposes a "best-effort truncate" policy that asks the server for a compressed summary if resume fails.

References / inspiration:
- prior internal doc: compact-transcript-schema (see linked_artifacts)
- earlier streaming fallback notes (Phil C. Slack thread)
